Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). The owner just reviewed live screenshots of the NxLabs mod store and flagged three real issues. IMPORTANT: three other background agents are concurrently building GitHub/Thunderstore/Steam-Workshop import pipelines right now — do NOT touch `scripts/import-github-catalog.ts`, `scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts`, any new Steam Workshop import script, or `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `resolveUrl()`/`RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` — those files are owned by concurrent work and touching them will cause conflicts. Everything in this task is UI/display-layer plus a targeted description backfill on EXISTING already-imported rows, not sourcing pipeline work.

## Issue 1: Marketing /mods homepage hero doesn't match the approved mockup

Current live state (screenshot provided by owner): the hero image (`/nxlabs/hero-collage.png`) renders letterboxed/constrained on the right side of the hero block, with plain text on the left and a stats row below. The owner wants it **stretched full-width like the actual mockup**, with a transparent gradient overlay so text can sit legibly over the art, and "maybe some particle effect."

- Read `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/hero-collage.png` and `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/marketing-home.png` (the real approved mockups) carefully — match their actual hero treatment (full-bleed image, gradient/overlay direction, where text sits on top of the art vs. beside it).
- Current implementation is in `app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx` using `PageHero` from `components/marketing/primitives.tsx`. Read `PageHero`'s current implementation in full — determine whether it can be extended with a "full-bleed background art with overlay" variant, or whether this specific hero needs its own bespoke markup (check if any other marketing page already does a full-bleed hero-with-overlay treatment you can follow as precedent, e.g. the main homepage).
- Particle effect: keep it tasteful and lightweight — a small canvas-based ambient particle field (like slow-drifting motes/embers, matching a mod-store/tech aesthetic) is fine, but respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (disable/freeze it for users who set that), and it must not block the hero image or text from being visible immediately on load (no gating behind client JS — this exact page had a real bug earlier today where a scroll-reveal wrapper made the hero invisible; don't reintroduce that class of bug).
- This is the MARKETING page. Do a matching pass on the portal's `/dashboard/nxlabs` hero too (uses `PageShell`'s `heroImage` slot) ONLY if it can adopt a similar treatment without breaking the Nexion portal shell's chrome (navy/violet sidebar layout) — portal pages have real layout constraints marketing doesn't (no full-bleed background, fixed content width against the sidebar). Check `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/portal-home.png` for what the PORTAL-specific hero treatment should look like (it may legitimately be different/more contained than marketing's, and that's fine — don't force marketing's exact treatment into the portal shell if the mockup shows something else for the portal).

## Issue 2: Mod detail pages have NO game hero image at all

Screenshot shows the CounterStrikeSharp mod detail page (`/mods/cs2/counterstrikesharp` or similar) with just plain text header ("NxLabs / CounterStrikeSharp / C# plugin runtime most CS2 plugins need. / NxLabs / Counter-Strike 2") and no visual at all.

- The correct game-specific hero art already exists and is used correctly elsewhere: `GAME_ART_SLUG[family].hero` (confirmed correct today for rust/valheim/cs2/palworld/minecraft — see `app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx` for how the per-family browse page already uses it correctly).
- Add the matching game's hero image to BOTH mod detail page routes: `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx` and `app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`. Read both files in full first. This should look like a real page header treatment (hero art behind/beside the mod name + its own icon), not just slapping the giant family hero above everything redundantly — look at how the per-family browse page balances "big game hero" + "grid of individual mod cards with their own icons" for the right visual hierarchy, and adapt that same balance for a detail page (game hero as backdrop/context, mod's own icon/name as the foreground focus).

## Issue 3: Some mods have thin or missing descriptions

Real example from the screenshot: CounterStrikeSharp's description is just "C# plugin runtime most CS2 plugins need." — that's the GitHub repo's short one-line `description` field, nothing more.

- Investigate PER SOURCE (Modrinth, GitHub, Thunderstore, Spiget/uMod — check `GameMod.source` values currently in the DB) whether a richer real field exists that ISN'T currently being captured/displayed:
  - Modrinth: their API has both a short `description` (tagline) and a longer `body` (full markdown project page content) — check if `body` is being fetched/stored anywhere and displayed, or if only the short tagline made it in. If `body` exists and isn't shown, that's a real, quick win — display it (rendered as safe markdown-to-text or a trimmed excerpt, your call on formatting) on the detail page without needing to touch the import pipeline (a new script reading existing already-stored data, or check if `body` was even captured in the first import — if it wasn't captured at all, you may need a small NON-conflicting backfill script that only ADDS a new field/updates existing modrinth rows via their read-only `/project/{id}` endpoint, but do NOT touch `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts` itself, write a separate one-off backfill script instead so you don't conflict with anything).
  - GitHub-sourced mods (the CounterStrikeSharp example): the concurrent GitHub-import agent is actively building this pipeline right now and its description field is exactly the repo's one-line `description` — this is real, honest data (that's genuinely all GitHub's repo metadata offers for a one-liner) so there isn't a "hidden longer field" the way Modrinth has `body`. For these, don't fabricate marketing copy. Instead check whether the repo's README (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/readme` or raw content) has a real usable intro paragraph you could extract as a longer description — but ONLY do this as a note in your report for the GitHub import agent to consider (do not implement it yourself since you'd be touching their in-progress file); for THIS task, focus on Modrinth's `body` field as the real quick win, and if other sources have similar "already-fetched-but-unused" richer fields, use those too.
  - Confirm via a real DB check (script under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts`, `npx tsx`, delete after — NEVER print a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string) how many active mods currently have a null/empty `description` and break that down by source, so you know the real scope before deciding what's worth fixing now vs. flagging for later.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read every file mentioned above in full before editing.
- Any DB backfill script is a one-off under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` or a properly named new script if it's meant to be re-run later (e.g. `scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts`) — dry-run by default, idempotent.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Real Playwright before/after screenshots comparing against the actual mockup files in `.design-refs/nxlabs/`.
- Build via `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (never build directly in /opt/nxeon), verify staging HTTP 200 + visually correct, then `bash scripts/promote-production.sh`, confirm BUILD_ID changed + fresh service ActiveEnterTimestamp.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- Commit, confirm it reached `origin/main`.

Report back: what the hero treatment ended up looking like vs. the mockup (with reasoning for any deliberate deviation), confirmation mod detail pages now show real game hero art on both marketing and portal, and real before/after numbers on the description backfill (how many mods gained a real, non-fabricated longer description).

## NxLabs ModCard — footer download/order-server row, real box-art game badge (2026-09-20)

**Why.** Owner review of a live screenshot of the mod card (`components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, used
across `/mods`, `/mods/games/[family]`, and `/dashboard/nxlabs`) flagged three concrete issues: the
"No matching server yet — order one" prompt sat as plain link text *outside* the card; there was no
download action or downloads-count stat despite `GameMod.downloads` already being real, populated
data; and the corner game-identifier badge was a 24x24 crop of the flat wordmark logo — "so small you
can't even see it."

**What changed.**
- `ModCard` now renders as an outer `<div class="card">` wrapping the clickable `<Link>` (image +
  name/description, unchanged) plus a new footer row *inside* the card's own boundary but as a
  sibling of the `<Link>` — real `<button>`/`<select>` elements can't legally nest inside an `<a>`.
  The footer holds two independent slots: a download button (new `download` prop) and a
  server-availability action (new `footer` prop, a `React.ReactNode`).
- **Download button + count.** `StoreBrowser` resolves `resolveDownloadUrl()` — the exact function
  the mod detail page's own "Download file"/"View on X" button already calls — for the whole current
  page's mods in parallel (`Promise.all`), then passes each result into its `ModCard`. Same real
  per-source destination (Modrinth CDN, Thunderstore package, Spiget, GitHub release, ...) as the
  detail page; no new resolution mechanism. `ModSummary` (`lib/mods-catalog.ts`) now also carries
  `url`/`sourceId`/`appliesToVariant` — the three fields `resolveDownloadUrl()` needs — so a browse
  grid doesn't need a second per-mod query (`queryCatalogMods` already loads the full `GameMod` row
  internally; exposing these on the summary type is free). The downloads-count stat itself
  (`formatDownloads`) was already on the card; only the button is new.
- **"No matching server" footer.** Moved inside the card, shortened to "No matching server" +
  a real "Order server" button — a visual sibling of the existing `QuickAddButton` "eligible server"
  case (same footer row, same button sizing/weight), not a redesign. Still portal-only
  (`StoreBrowser`'s `serversByFamily` prop) — the public `/mods` pages render the card with just its
  download button and no server-action row, same as before.
- **Real box-art badge.** `components/mods/GameBadge.tsx` now renders the game's real portrait poster
  art (`GAME_ART_SLUG[family].poster`, the same asset `GameCoverTile`/the game-servers carousel use)
  at 44x64px instead of the old 24x24 wordmark crop, falling back to the hero still and then the old
  wordmark for the handful of "Wave 3 SCAFFOLD" families with no real key-art yet. Its border color is
  genuinely sampled from that same image file — `lib/game-poster-color.ts` (new) uses `sharp`'s own
  per-channel `.stats()` mean (the same "average color" a devtools eyedropper-over-the-whole-image
  would show), then nudges only the *lightness* into a legible band (25–70%) so a mostly-dark or
  mostly-white poster still reads as a border; hue/saturation stay exactly what the image produced.
  Computed once per family and cached in an in-memory `Map` for the life of the server process — the
  art files never change at runtime, so there's no reason to re-decode the same jpeg on every card
